svg.title: Call, return and the stack
svg.desc: Four panels for the Lab 07 theory. 1: fact(3) in ember from the ISA §6 listing: five snapshots of the stack 0xFFF…0xFF7 at trace steps 2, 11, 27, 30 and 34; CALL pushes the return address, PUSH A saves n, frames of fact(3), fact(2), fact(1); POP and RET only raise SP and the old bytes stay. 2: in C++ every call of fact has its own n, and the values come back as 1, 2, 6. 3: passing by value, by pointer and by reference. 4: the stack as a type: top is the last used slot, SP is the next free one.
svg.text: CALL is a jump that remembers where to come back to. It remembers on the stack.
1. fact(3) in ember: the stack step by step
The listing from ISA §6, only with LOADI A, 3. Step numbers come from the trace of ./run.sh 09 a=3 in the Lab 07 practice.
CALL pushes the address after itself: low byte first, then high (05, 00). RET pops them in reverse order. PUSH A saves n: the next call will overwrite A.
POP and RET erase nothing, they only raise SP. Grey cells are old values, to be overwritten by the next PUSH.
After fact(3) SP is back at 0xFFF: every PUSH has its POP, every CALL its RET. Convention: argument and result in A.
2. Every call has its own n
Three different n in three different frames; each lives until its call returns.
A global g_n instead of a parameter: one box for every call, and fact(4) = 1.
it has no box of its own:
r is another name for a
const T& is like T&, but read-only: writing through it does not compile.
4. The stack as a type: the same LIFO, counted differently
